assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the three REVIEWED items curated on konosuba:megumin@original-light-novel at basis_commit, each read in full: #main-principal-monograph (the active_provisional main-only MAIN01-MAIN17 monograph, with paragraph-level locators and the CP06 M01-M06 and J01 adjudications it reports), #expanded-monograph (the active_provisional EXPANDED_V1 monograph over the Explosions 01-03 prequels, Continued Explosions 01-02, the game-derived Fantastic Days novel and individually dispositioned artbook, comic and TRPG components) and #stage-d-principal-model (the active_provisional POST_VALIDATION_STAGE_D_V1 reconstruction specification with its four SD1 working commitments). The KonoSuba CURRENT_STATE_AND_CORPUS_MAP.md was read for method, authority order and gate state only. The MAIN_ONLY_R1 model, the executed 90-first suite and its diagnostic report, the core freeze, the model-evidence matrix, the extended synthesis, the sequential readings, ledgers, checkpoints, the voice sheet and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them; outcomes the monographs themselves report (for example CP06 M02 CONFIRMED, M05 AMBIGUOUS) are read as reported, and the model's MODERATE and LOW labels are inputs, not conclusions. Holdout, adaptation and post-MAIN17 material is excluded, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The main sequence from MAIN01 recruitment (C1P461-482) through the MAIN17 ending and gift (FP734-740), plus prequel slices in the Crimson Demon village (Explosions 01-03) and the separately provenanced Continued Explosions 01-02 and Fantastic Days episodes, each kept as its own slice; the expanded books were read after main and holdout exposure, so they qualify the account but are not prospective tests, and prequel narration grants no later relationship knowledge. The model has no single default state and requires chronology, state, means and decision interval to be specified first. No state after MAIN17 is established and no in-world dates are fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The main monograph argues a governing conflict between a chosen art and a needed place among particular people, mediated by appraisals of contribution, humiliation, target meaning, reward and loss (sections 1, 3-4, 9); the Stage D model turns this into typed appraisals (section 8), rewards and aversions (9), error generators (10) and an operational procedure (14), and the expanded monograph adds pre-discovery reconsideration (EXP01 U043P0288-0441). B was rejected because the model's own selector under grave risk is OPEN (SD1-M04), its other commitments are MODERATE or LOW, CP06 M01 and M06 are PARTIAL and M05 AMBIGUOUS, and the executed suite is not curated here. D was rejected because the appraisal structure is explicit, located and bounded by named countercases.

The main monograph's section 12 table traces PRESERVE, STRENGTHEN and OPEN transitions with routes and confidences across MAIN01-MAIN17 (the V05 F169-219 and V16 F399-408 consideration episodes, the V09-V17 relationship steps, growing control from MAIN02 to the V17 barrage), and the expanded monograph adds prequel reconsideration before the fortunate card discovery while firewalling prequel from main knowledge. A was rejected because nothing after MAIN17 is established, the expanded slices were read post-exposure and the durability of reconsideration is open (model section 26). C was rejected because the transitions are explicit, located and separated from adjacent states.

Section 10 of the main monograph gives six located witnesses with speaker, addressee and state (爆裂魔法しか使えないです and 私は爆裂魔法しか愛せない at MAIN01 C1P461/479, お守り at MAIN09 C1P61/116, それ〝も〟あだ名 at MAIN09 FP537, 仲間以上恋人未満 at MAIN11 Ep), says formal endings do not imply deference, and keeps the J01 specialist and relational branches with recorded disagreement; model sections 15 and 19 give a functional voice grammar. B was rejected because the forms are few, the voice ledger and 392-slot voice sheet are not curated here, and the model itself says generated Japanese does not establish voice accuracy. D was rejected because exact forms are tied to audience and state.

Located ordinary conduct includes practical use of beginner magic (MAIN01 C2), gathering and cooking well enough to teach Iris with an invented family recipe (V10), remittances, coupons and limits on money sent home, the daily Explosion walk with Kazuma (V09-V11 locators), Komekko's care and prequel breakfasts and food brought home; model section 18 warns against forcing every inconvenience into performance. B was rejected because these are summarized from uncurated ledgers and no routine, schedule or preference inventory is given. D was rejected because the ordinary acts are located and paired with their limits.

Recipient-specific conduct is located across phases for Kazuma (carrying, V09 reciprocal liking, V10 jealousy, the V11 仲間以上恋人未満 proposal, V12 acceptance, V16 private advance, V17 gift and acknowledged learning), Yunyun (main and prequel rivalry, care and exploitation, missed invitations), Darkness (amulet, V17 C1P185-194 compromise with exact actors, the C3P425-438 shield promise), Iris, Komekko and Wolbach, with model section 16 keeping each companion's own agency. A was rejected because exclusivity and negotiated limits remain open, the evidence is one project's same-assistant analysis and no controlled recipient comparison exists. C was rejected because at least five relations carry multi-phase, located conditioning with exact actor ordering.

Megumin's own first-person epilogue in V09 confirms desire while preserving uncertainty, and the prequels supply her narration of embarrassment, pride, selective hearing and admitted inference (expanded section 7); main section 11 separates Kazuma's inferences from her interior, for example her reading of his room choice in V11 and her identification of the hidden Darkness in V16. B was rejected because most main-series interior is mediated by Kazuma's narration and her own narration does not verify the causes she assigns to others. D was rejected because direct, located first-person access exists.

Identity defense against ordinary cost (V09 imitation disposal, the V13 F221-232 attempted chant, the V15 summons), the EXP02 cat shield after a status taunt, the V17 C3P425-438 acceptance of possible mutual death and the Wolbach disruption are located, and SD1-M01 states a MODERATE bounded expectation for received denigration with ordinary cost. B was rejected because CP06 M01 is PARTIAL, M05 AMBIGUOUS and SD1-M04 OPEN, so the priority under grave risk cannot be predicted. D was rejected because the trigger distinctions and adverse branches are explicit and located.

Reasoned reconsideration is located before outcome: the V05 advanced-magic request that Kazuma overrides against her intention (F219), V16 F399-408, EXP01's prepared sacrifice before the card discovery and Continued01 U019P283-319 where an accepted leader responsibility stops a raid; SD1-M02 and SD1-M03 bound these as MODERATE and MODERATE-to-LOW. B was rejected because the same evidence shows concern failing to inhibit (EXP02, V17 overload and shared death) with no identified selector. D was rejected because these are her own reconsiderations, not only the analyst's moral reading.

Crimson Demon theatricality as a controllable social language (main section 2), the invented secret recipe, preferring to lose face before Komekko rather than humiliate Kazuma, teasing and pointed rebuttal, and model section 20's humor envelope with the H1-H4 literalness classes retained. B was rejected because the humor ledger is not curated here and the repertoire is described more than quoted. D was rejected because the play is located and bounded by its costs.

The main monograph declares the admitted 137-member MAIN01-MAIN17 principal text contract, the 66-artifact freeze, 1,701 bounded-check slots across 17 members, that V01-V13 were retrieved through accepted analyses rather than newly reread, and the excluded afterwords, holdouts, expanded and adaptation material; the expanded monograph declares its admitted components and post-exposure reading. A was rejected because readings, ledgers and sources are outside this evidence set and V01-V13 were not freshly read. C was rejected because the boundary is exact and itemized.

Affirmative located limitations: the V09 imitation disposed of despite known cost, V09 raids continuing past the stopping point, V17 C1P183-185 desired further fire under overload, V17 C3P425-438 accepted mutual death, the EXP02 cat thrown toward the target after Yunyun's warning, the Fantastic Days cart destroyed after a received instruction, the Continued02 false Iris cover, and model section 28's rejected caricatures. A was rejected because the formal M05 result is AMBIGUOUS and all of this is one project's analysis. C was rejected because these are located counterinstances rather than gaps.

Model section 5 lists state variables (spells and control, points, mana, bodily load, geometry, accepted responsibilities, negotiated limits) and slice firewalls, and the main monograph fixes exact intra-scene orderings (V16 C3P319-322, V17 C1P185-194, MAIN05 F219). B was rejected because there is no default state or selector set, in-world dates of the prequel and Continued material are not fixed and the time of acquiring incantation-free control is explicitly undated. D was rejected because state variables and orderings are explicit.

conditions: Short, situated turns in a named phase and attested relationship, with chronology, mode, state and audience specified first.
Polite structure is used for its function (technical explanation, dramatic introduction, rebuttal, reluctant request, refusal, responsibility admission), never as a deference or kindness switch.
No compulsory chant, catchphrase, destructive ending or status insult in a neutral exchange; a spell name or ritual is not a completed cast.
Output is labeled noncanonical, written only, and makes no acoustic or native-voice claim.
scenario_readiness.note: Model sections 15 and 19 give a social-script and voice grammar and the main monograph supplies located forms with audience and state. READY was rejected because exact forms are few, generated Japanese is explicitly not voice-accuracy evidence and the J01 relational branch retains disagreement; NOT_READY was rejected because the grammar and located forms do constrain a short situated turn.

conditions: The probe states chronology, state, means, target and provider permissions and keeps desire, attempt, execution, recovery and aftermath as separate stages.
Under grave collateral or relational risk, rival outcomes are prebound and neither restraint nor casting is predicted (SD1-M04 OPEN).
In transfer, magic is removed without inventing weapons, explosives or professional expertise; any analogous cherished craft must be supplied and carries lower mapping confidence.
Companions keep their own information, skills and refusals; no relationship endpoint beyond MAIN17 is assumed.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named slice: a prequel phase in the Crimson Demon village (Explosions 01-03), a Continued Explosions or Fantastic Days episode as its own slice, or a main-sequence phase from MAIN01 recruitment to the MAIN17 ending; never after MAIN17, and prequel slices without later relationship knowledge.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Attested relations in their phase-appropriate state: Kazuma as carrier, companion and negotiated partner, Yunyun as rival and friend, Darkness, Aqua, Iris, Komekko, Wolbach as teacher-linked target, or strangers as audience, client or opponent without fabricated shared history.
setting_constraints: Source-world adventuring, village, household or royal settings of the admitted main and expanded slices
A supplied realistic transfer setting with magic removed and no substitute weapons or expertise
Finite mana, bodily depletion and provider dependence retained
Open domains, including grave-risk priority and post-MAIN17 states, end in abstention

scenario_readiness.note: Model sections 21 and 22 define canonical-comic and cross-context transfer modes, and SD1-M01 to SD1-M03 give bounded working expectations with typed adverse outcomes. READY was rejected because SD1-M04 is OPEN and no curated independent test exists; NOT_READY was rejected because the transfer rules, state variables and rejection list are explicit.

conditions: Scenes of attested kinds: cooking and gathering, small household economies, family care, rivalry visits, the daily cast and walk, gifts.
No favorite food, schedule or domestic routine beyond what is located; scarcity explains resource attention without making every expenditure prudent.
A minor criticism is not treated as denial of her art, and a neutral task contains no compulsory cast.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary conduct is located and model section 18 permits meals, work, small economies, rivalry and affection without forcing performance. READY was rejected because no routine or preference inventory exists; NOT_READY was rejected because the located ordinary acts constrain a scene.

conditions: Only for a self-accepted contribution burden with a known feasible alternative, or an explicitly accepted responsibility with a received explanation and real alternative.
Meaningful consideration is expected, not actual purchase, permanent reform or a guaranteed outcome.
External prevention is never scored as voluntary restraint, and later rescue or praise never authorizes an earlier start.
Grave-risk choices are not predicted in either direction.
scenario_readiness.note: SD1-M02 and SD1-M03 bound reconsideration under a self-accepted contribution burden or an accepted responsibility, with located precedents. READY was rejected because concern demonstrably fails in other branches and the grave-risk selector is open; NOT_READY was rejected because the two bounded triggers are explicit, located and typed.

conditions: Toward Kazuma only, in a named main-series phase, with the step reached by then (V09 reciprocal liking, V11 proposal, V12 accepted intermediate relation, V16 private advance).
No marriage, completed sex, stable exclusive household or universal consent is assumed; consent is specific to a moment and act.
Darkness and Iris remain rivals and companions in their own right, and Ragcraft's impersonation is not Megumin's conduct.
No romance is imported into prequel slices.
scenario_readiness.note: The Kazuma relationship is located step by step from V09 to V17 with negotiated boundaries and act-specific consent, and model section 16 keeps exclusivity unsettled. READY was rejected because the endpoints are explicitly open; NOT_READY was rejected because the progression is precise and recipient-specific.

conditions: Party or small-group adventuring, leadership of the Continued Explosions kind, or item identification and practical reasoning; no institutional command.
Mana, transport, target separation and recovery are supplied by named providers before the act and are never reconstructed from a successful blast.
Successful damage does not certify a prepared safe operation, and sole authorship of a distributed victory is not assigned.
scenario_readiness.note: Adventuring artillery within distributed operations (MAIN02 Destroyer relay, V06, V09, V13-V17), Continued Explosions leadership and item identification, and the Fantastic Days final operation are located, and model section 11 maps competence and dependencies. READY was rejected because CP06 M03 safe-artillery preparation is NOT_TESTED and outcomes are distributed; NOT_READY was rejected because the competence map and its dependencies are explicit.

known_limits.statement: The priority under known grave collateral danger, art reward and a valued shield promise is OPEN in the model (SD1-M04); the formal CP06 M05 result is AMBIGUOUS and M06 PARTIAL, while EXP02 and MAIN17 C3P425-438 prevent any universal affection brake.
CP06 M03 is NOT_TESTED: a fully prepared operation with safe friendly geometry, resources and exit or recovery planning is not established, and successful damage or a later carry does not supply it.
Target-specific friction rests on the Wolbach episode; CP06 M04 is NOT_TESTED in V16-V17, and a bonded opponent differs from a companion at collateral risk or an animal used as a shield.

No marriage, completed sex or stable exclusive household is established with Kazuma; Kazuma's V05 point allocation was against Megumin's stated intention and later joy does not convert it into prior consent.

The expanded books were read after main and holdout exposure; they qualify the account but are not prospective tests, fourteen holdout contracts were untested, and prequel narration grants no later relationship knowledge.

Several apparent stops are other people's acts (Darkness catching her at V17 C1P185, Yunyun catching the cat in EXP02, a crowd disarming her in Fantastic Days); they are not evidence of voluntary inhibition.

The Stage D commitments are source-known diagnostic working generalizations requiring prebound premises; the model states that no plausible generated answer earns independent accuracy, VERY_HIGH fidelity or a numerical moral-development level.

Fantastic Days is game-derived, the artbook dungeon wish is an attributed imagined preference, and the TRPG Crimson Mage sample sheets are source-local personas; none adds biography, learned skills or audio evidence.

The executed suite, diagnostic report, core freeze, evidence matrix, MAIN_ONLY_R1 model, readings, ledgers, checkpoints and sources are not curated on this subject and were not assessed, and holdout, adaptation and post-MAIN17 material is outside the boundary; missing support is not evidence that any trait or capacity is absent.
